title: Find the Repeated Number

concept.title: An array as a chain of jumps
body: You get `m` numbers, all between 1 and `m - 1`. By the pigeonhole principle some number repeats. Treat the array as a "jump table": from position `i` you jump to position `a[i]`. Because every value is a valid position and the value 0 is never a target, following the jumps from position 0 must eventually enter a **cycle**, and the entrance of the cycle is exactly the repeated number (two different positions jump to it).

body.code:
slow = fast = 0
while True:
    slow = a[slow]
    fast = a[a[fast]]
    if slow == fast: break
slow = 0
while slow != fast:
    slow = a[slow]
    fast = a[fast]
# slow is the repeated number

body: This is Floyd's "tortoise and hare" idea: the hare moves twice as fast; when they meet, restarting one of them from the beginning and moving both one step at a time makes them meet again at the entrance of the cycle. It uses no extra memory and does not change the array.

statement: You are given `m` integers, each between 1 and `m - 1`. Exactly one value occurs more than once (it may occur many times); every other value occurs once or not at all. Print the repeated value.
hints: Think of position `i` as pointing to position `a[i]`.
Starting at position 0 you must run into a cycle; use a slow and a fast pointer to meet inside it.
After they meet, restart one pointer from position 0 and move both by one step: they meet at the repeated value.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

m = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

# Your code here

explanation: The jumps `i -> a[i]` form a path that ends in a cycle, and the cycle starts at the repeated value. Floyd's algorithm finds the start of the cycle with two pointers.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

m = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

slow = fast = 0
while True:
    slow = a[slow]
    fast = a[a[fast]]
    if slow == fast:
        break
slow = 0
while slow != fast:
    slow = a[slow]
    fast = a[fast]
print(slow)
